explain.say: Over 2000 years ago, the Greek thinker Archimedes stepped into his bath, saw the water rise, and shouted "Eureka!", meaning "I found it!" He had found a way to measure the volume of odd shapes. Let us use his trick to find a stone's density, step by step.

explain.say: 54 grams, yes! Next, fill a eureka can, a can with a spout on the side, until water just drips out. Then gently lower the stone in on a thread. Look at the fourth step: water spills out of the spout into a measuring cylinder. Why does water come out?

explain.say: Because the stone pushes it out! The spilled water has exactly the same volume as the stone: 20 cubic centimetres. This is called displacement, which means pushing aside. Now the last step: density is mass divided by volume. Ready for the sum?

explain.say: 54 divided by 20 is 2.7 grams per cubic centimetre. Superb work! That matches granite, a common rock. Wow fact: gold is about 19 grams per cubic centimetre, which is how Archimedes could check if a crown was pure gold. Challenge: try this with a toy at home using a jug.

faq.q: How do you find the mass?
faq.a: Put the object on a top-pan balance or digital scale and read its mass in grams.
A eureka can, or displacement can, has a spout near the top. When you lower an object in, the water it pushes out flows into a measuring cylinder.

faq.q: Why does the spilled water equal the stone's volume?
faq.a: The stone takes up space in the can and pushes out exactly its own volume of water.
asks: How do you measure the volume of a stone?

faq.a: Divide the mass by the volume. 54 grams divided by 20 cubic centimetres gives 2.7 grams per cubic centimetre.
Archimedes realised that an object put in water pushes out its own volume of water, and that objects are pushed up by the weight of water they displace.

facts: The volume of water displaced equals the volume of the fully submerged object.
Granite has a density of about 2.7 g/cm³; gold about 19.3 g/cm³.

quiz.say: A stone of mass 90 g pushes 30 cm³ of water out of a eureka can. Its density?
quiz.show: A stone of mass 90 g pushes 30 cm³ of water out of a eureka can. Its density?

wrong.0: That multiplies; density is mass divided by volume.
wrong.2: That divides volume by mass, the wrong way round.

quiz.say: Why must the eureka can be filled until water drips from the spout first?

options.show: So all displaced water is caught

quiz.why: If the can starts full to the spout, every bit of water the stone pushes aside flows out to be measured.

wrong.0: The water level does not change the stone's mass.
